supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40:19–13:40:22 UTC, paul.becker authenticated to WS-DREYES-01 from 10.52.10.23, and the workstation recorded the resulting network logon under paul.becker.

At 13:41:32 UTC, PowerShell ran on WS-DREYES-01 as paul.becker with the command `-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \\FILE-COP-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1`; this matches the organization’s stated workstation-patching procedure.
The same PowerShell process connected through the proxy to download.windowsupdate.com, followed by wusa installing a Windows update package; these events are consistent with patching.
The administrator’s PowerShell process exited at 13:41:57 UTC.

Explorer updated dan.reyes’s UserAssist entry with a ROT13-encoded path that decodes to powershell.exe at 13:30:56 and again at 13:42:23 UTC. These entries do not establish the process command line or conclusively identify the reported window.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records show the authorized administrator’s PowerShell command line and related patch activity, but do not establish whether that process was the window dan.reyes reported.
The UserAssist records are registry updates, not direct process-creation records; they do not provide command-line arguments or prove the exact time a PowerShell process started.
No PowerShell script contents, execution transcript, or console/window visibility evidence is provided.
claims_not_established: Whether the reported PowerShell window was the authorized patching process, a separate PowerShell launch by dan.reyes, or another event.
Whether the PowerShell activity indicated by the UserAssist entries was benign or malicious.
What the patch script did beyond the activity visible in the provided records.
additional_evidence_needed: Endpoint process telemetry around 13:20–14:20 UTC, including any records for PowerShell launched under dan.reyes and its parent process and command line.
PowerShell operational or script-block logs, transcripts, and the contents and integrity details of \\FILE-COP-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1.
Remote-administration or management-tool logs from WS-PBECKER-01 that can correlate paul.becker’s session with the reported window.
Follow-up with dan.reyes about the window’s timing and appearance.
unrelated_findings: Google Drive File Stream started on WS-DREYES-01 at 14:14:40 UTC. The inventory lists Microsoft 365/OneDrive as approved and no other cloud-storage services, so review this separately; it does not determine the alerted PowerShell activity. (T134-00261, T134-00262)

dan.reyes ran `cmd.exe /c wmic process list brief` at 14:01 UTC. This is outside the immediate reported window and is not linked by the available evidence to the PowerShell alert; review separately if warranted. (T134-00235, T134-00236)
